excluded_lineages: its FIFO compaction, group reset, listener-harness and canonical-spec descendants

decisions.summary: Web IM relay and external channels already converge on a shared Gateway inbound path, with /stop as the existing narrow text-control precedent.

accepted_outcomes: The candidate discovers the shared inbound, trigger-normalization, reply-routing and shadow behavior without asking the user where commands are parsed.
It starts from the shared seam or gives concrete evidence for an equally coherent adjacent owner; it does not create unrelated Feishu-only semantics.
rejected_outcomes: Independent Web IM and Feishu implementations that can disagree on session-control meaning.
A second channel-specific control service without repository evidence.

decisions.summary: The kernel already exposes manual compaction through agent.sdk and owns transcript compaction semantics.

accepted_outcomes: The design reuses or minimally extends the public compact path and derives success, no-op and failure behavior from the transcript lifecycle.
Any compact guidance remains an input to compaction rather than an ordinary conversational turn.
rejected_outcomes: A second Gateway-side summarizer or personal_assistant importing agent.core.
Treating an ordinary user turn as equivalent to a durable compaction boundary.

decisions.summary: The brief requires new-session and user-initiated compaction semantics across both internal Web IM and Feishu, with independent authoring followed by one owner review.

accepted_outcomes: Both channels expose the same two product capabilities and user-visible outcomes in the final spec/design.
The candidate resolves repository facts and consolidates product choices in the promised unified review instead of serially asking for permission to analyze each channel.
rejected_outcomes: Supporting only one channel or only one of the two requested capabilities.
Claiming competitor behavior as evidence when the snapshot provides no verifiable competitor source.
oracle.acceptance_notes: The absent competitor corpus is an evidence limitation, not a reason to block or invent findings.

decisions.summary: Starting a fresh Agent context must preserve the human-visible chat timeline and change only future model context.

accepted_outcomes: The spec preserves visible messages in the existing chat and makes the next ordinary turn independent of the old Agent context.
The candidate explains the visible-history versus fresh-context boundary and applies the pre-frozen historical owner answer after surfacing the value fork.
rejected_outcomes: Deleting or hiding visible history, or creating a different IM/Feishu chat as the default meaning of /new.
oracle.acceptance_notes: The cutoff world does not uniquely decide visible-history behavior. The historical owner answer is resolved and replayable, but the candidate still has to surface the product fork; it is not a retrievable F.

decisions.summary: Choose how a group-chat participant explicitly targets a shared Agent context for state-changing controls.

accepted_outcomes: The final review explains shared group-context ownership, compares accidental-trigger risk with convenience, and recommends a clear mention/reply/permission rule.
Explicit mention/reply targeting can receive full credit, but another rule can also pass if it prevents ambiguous shared-state mutation and fits cutoff trigger semantics.
rejected_outcomes: Silently allowing unrelated unaddressed group text to reset or compact shared context.
Inventing per-user group sessions as an incidental implementation detail.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Judge clarity and safety of the chosen rule, not the historical bare-/stop exception.

decisions.summary: Choose observable ordering for new-session and compaction when work is active or queued.

accepted_outcomes: The final review compares interrupt, reject and queue behavior for each control and recommends an unambiguous rule for prior and later ordinary messages.

Immediate-abandon new plus FIFO compact is acceptable, but so are other explicit semantics that preserve context integrity, never let later input overtake an accepted compact, and communicate the result truthfully.
rejected_outcomes: Opportunistic context mutation concurrent with an active run.
Accepting compact for later execution while allowing a subsequently received ordinary message to overtake it.
oracle.acceptance_notes: The post-design FIFO defect is a conditional behavior probe, not a requirement to reproduce the historical queue implementation.

decisions.summary: A successful fresh-context boundary cannot admit old queued input into the new context or show old-run output after success; a failed reset cannot destroy the old world.

accepted_outcomes: The design gives one complete linearization argument for active, queued and steered input plus every user-visible output path it discovers.

Success, failure and restart states preserve their stated binding/history guarantees; generation checks, cancellation tokens, transactional publication or an equivalent mechanism can all receive full credit.
rejected_outcomes: Only cancelling the current Kernel run while queued old input can submit on the new context.
Suppressing only final output while stream/intermediate/external output can appear after the new-session confirmation.
Reset failure that loses the old binding, visible history or already accepted output without an explicit outcome.
oracle.acceptance_notes: Do not require historical lease, generation, field or class names; require an equivalent complete proof.

decisions.summary: Current coordinator, binder, SDK and shadow components already separate transition, binding, kernel and external-projection ownership.

accepted_outcomes: The design assigns each state transition to the existing owner or justifies a smaller/deeper replacement that preserves package boundaries and a single source of truth.
It follows actual composition and persistence paths instead of drawing an architecture disconnected from cutoff code.
rejected_outcomes: Inbound parsing directly mutating durable bindings or bypassing the kernel SDK.
A parallel external recovery/outbox system with overlapping authority and no migration rationale.

decisions.summary: Provider retries and process crashes must not repeat a state-changing reset/compact or permanently lose/contradict its visible result.

accepted_outcomes: A stable ingress identity or equivalent existing guarantee protects the state change itself, not only the reply text.
The design states how an accepted result reaches the triggering channel and shadow conversation across retry/restart, and states any at-least-once limitation honestly.
One-store, recoverable handoff, idempotent replay or another design can receive full credit when its failure table proves convergence.
rejected_outcomes: Confirmation deduplication used as a substitute for operation idempotency.
A crash window that can silently apply the state change twice or strand a committed result with no recovery path.
Claiming provider exactly-once behavior unsupported by the cutoff system.
oracle.acceptance_notes: The historical operation ledger and pending-intent materializer are examples, not mandatory topology.

decisions.summary: Choose the smallest discoverable interaction and grammar that can express both controls consistently across Web IM and Feishu.

accepted_outcomes: The final review compares text-only commands with any proposed UI affordance, recommends a bounded grammar/surface and explains discoverability plus compatibility costs.
Exact /new and /compact text can receive full credit, but a different minimal companion surface may also pass if Feishu parity and unambiguous parsing remain intact.
rejected_outcomes: An extensible command platform, alias family, history browser or new protocol surface added without present need.
Near-miss text unexpectedly mutating context because grammar and fallback-to-normal-message behavior are unspecified.

decisions.summary: Choose whether manual compaction accepts an optional focus and define truthful success, no-op and failure UX.

accepted_outcomes: The final review compares bare compaction with an optional free-form focus, recommends an in-scope choice and makes its added SDK/test cost visible.
Including focus may receive full credit, but deferring it may also receive full credit when bare manual compaction fully solves the brief and the scope rationale is strong.
Whatever scope is chosen, success, insufficient history, busy/deferred and failure are distinguishable; failure does not masquerade as successful context mutation.
rejected_outcomes: Silently adding focus as a normal user turn or presenting fallback output as a successful manual compact after the requested transformation failed.
Including or excluding focus without acknowledging the product and implementation trade-off.

decisions.summary: Gateway must use agent.sdk, IM must remain independent of agent, and the design must not restore a kernel HTTP control surface.

accepted_outcomes: The design derives and obeys current package boundaries without asking the user whether they apply.
A claimed need to cross a boundary is isolated as a new H decision with concrete evidence before dependent design proceeds.
rejected_outcomes: personal_assistant importing agent.core/platform, IM importing agent, or a new managed/remote kernel control endpoint.
